public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1108

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1108](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1108)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Nat Filter BigOperators

namespace Erdos1108

/--
The set $A = \left\{ \sum_{n\in S}n! : S\subset \mathbb{N}\text{ finite}\right\}$ of all finite
sums of distinct factorials.
-/
def FactorialSums : Set ℕ :=
  {m : ℕ | ∃ S : Finset ℕ, m = ∑ n ∈ S, n.factorial}

/--
A number is powerful if each prime factor appears with exponent at least 2.
-/
def IsPowerful (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → p ∣ n → p ^ 2 ∣ n
/--
For each $k \geq 2$, does the set $A = \left\{ \sum_{n\in S}n! : S\subset \mathbb{N}\text{ finite}\right\}$ of all finite sums of distinct factorials contain only finitely many $k$-th powers?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1108.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k ≥ 2,
    Set.Finite { a | a ∈ FactorialSums ∧ ∃ m : ℕ, m ^ k = a } := by
  sorry

/--
Does the set $A = \left\{ \sum_{n\in S}n! : S\subset \mathbb{N}\text{ finite}\right\}$ of all finite sums of distinct factorials contain only finitely many powerful numbers?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1108.parts.ii :
     answer(sorry) ↔ {a ∈ FactorialSums | IsPowerful a}.Finite := by
  sorry

end Erdos1108

findings.description: The factorial indices are unrestricted naturals, so a finset may contain both 0 and 1 and count the value 1 twice, since 0! = 1!. The source's factorial sums use positive indices. For example, Lean admits 4 = 0! + 1! + 2!, which is not a sum of distinct positive-index factorials. This enlarges the set by infinitely many values, not merely by the empty sum: every n! + 4 with n ≥ 3 belongs to the Lean set but not the intended set. Indeed, these values are 4 modulo 6, whereas positive-index factorial sums have residues only 0, 1, 2, or 3 modulo 6. Both `erdos_1108.parts.i` and `erdos_1108.parts.ii` consequently use the wrong set A.
findings.source_evidence: The cited page, https://www.erdosproblems.com/1108, asks the two finiteness questions for factorial sums indexed by finite subsets of ℕ. Its cited primary reference disambiguates the indexing: Brindza–Erdős, “On some Diophantine problems involving powers and factorials,” J. Austral. Math. Soc. Series A 51 (1991), p. 2, equation (2), uses ∑_{i=1}^∞ ε_i i!, with ε_i ∈ {0,1} and finite support (https://doi.org/10.1017/S1446788700033255). Erdős's earlier “Some personal and mathematical reminiscences of Kurt Mahler,” p. 2, likewise starts the factorial sums at i = 1 (https://renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1989-34.pdf).
findings.suggested_fix:
Require positive factorial indices, for example:
`def FactorialSums : Set ℕ := {m | ∃ S : Finset ℕ, (∀ n ∈ S, 0 < n) ∧ m = ∑ n ∈ S, n.factorial}`.
The empty finset may remain allowed; its contribution of 0 is harmless for both finiteness questions.

sources_consulted: Brindza and Erdős, On some Diophantine problems involving powers and factorials, J. Austral. Math. Soc. Series A 51 (1991), 1–7, §1: https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/S1446788700033255
Erdős, Some personal and mathematical reminiscences of Kurt Mahler, Austral. Math. Soc. Gaz. 16 (1989), 1–2: https://renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1989-34.pdf
review.notes: Checked all four declarations. The quantifier scopes, bounds, answer-slot polarity, and powerful-number predicate otherwise match the source. Both research-open tags agree with the current source. Lean experiments in /workspace/review/scratch.lean verify the small boundary cases, equivalence of IsPowerful with Nat.Powerful, and invariance of finiteness under removing 0. /workspace/review/indexing-proof.lean proves the infinite difference between the two factorial-sum sets; its proofs do not depend on sorryAx. No checkout files were changed.

demonstrated.claim: The implemented set contains 4 via the indices {0, 1, 2}, but no sum of factorials over distinct positive indices equals 4.

submission.summary: /workspace/review/trivial_proof.lean proves both sides of this concrete definition mismatch. It does not claim to settle either open finiteness question.

trivial_proof.lean:
import FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«1108»

/-!
The source's indices start at 1: Brindza–Erdős (1991), §1, equation (2).
Allowing both 0! and 1! counts the value 1 twice. This is a definition
counterexample, not a resolution of either open finiteness question.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

-- Erdos1108.FactorialSums: the implemented set contains 4 = 0! + 1! + 2!.
example : (4 : ℕ) ∈ Erdos1108.FactorialSums := by
  exact ⟨{0, 1, 2}, by norm_num⟩

-- Erdos1108.FactorialSums: the intended positive-index sums cannot equal 4.
example : ¬ ∃ S : Finset ℕ, (∀ n ∈ S, 0 < n) ∧ 4 = ∑ n ∈ S, n.factorial := by
  rintro ⟨S, hpos, hsum⟩
  have hS : S ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 4 := by
    intro n hn
    refine Finset.mem_Icc.mpr ⟨hpos n hn, ?_⟩
    calc
      n ≤ n.factorial := Nat.self_le_factorial n
      _ ≤ ∑ i ∈ S, i.factorial := Finset.single_le_sum (fun _ _ => Nat.zero_le _) hn
      _ = 4 := hsum.symm
  have checked : ∀ T ∈ (Finset.Icc 1 4).powerset, (∑ n ∈ T, n.factorial) ≠ 4 := by
    decide
  exact checked S (Finset.mem_powerset.mpr hS) hsum.symm

submission.summary: Restricted factorial indices to positive naturals, preventing simultaneous inclusion of 0! and 1!, and updated all three relevant docstrings. The empty sum remains allowed. The edited file compiles with only the expected `sorry` warnings; separate regression checks confirm that 0 and 9 belong to the corrected set and 4 does not.
